Business domain map

What Bunkai is for, how it earns, and what every domain term means. Reverse-engineered from upex-bunkai-tms at origin/staging commit 98ee1b4 (sections updated 2026-10-13); sections still dated 2026-10-02 were built at main commit e88512e. Every path below is relative to that repository; db:<table> is a table in supabase/migrations/; route:<path> is a page or API route of the app.

Overview

Confidence: Medium. What the product does is now verified in code at origin/staging 98ee1b4 (89 migrations, the /api/v1 handlers and the shipped screens): the gap the previous version recorded between docs and code (tests, runs, bugs, dashboards missing) is closed. The problem framing and the personas still come from marketing-toned in-repo docs, which keeps the synthesis at Medium.

Problem statement

Bunkai is a Test Management System (TMS). Its metadata reads "Open-core Test Management System. ATCs (Acceptance Test Cases), modular tests, full traceability" (app/layout.tsx). The product docs frame the problem as existing TMSs (Xray, Zephyr Scale, TestRail, qTest) acting as document vaults: duplicated steps across test cases, missing traceability from user story to test to bug, and pass-rate reports that do not say what is validated (.context/business/business-model.md, .context/PRD/executive-summary.md; marketing-toned prose, so confidence is downgraded).

The answer the code enforces is structural. An ATC cannot be created or updated without a user story and at least one of that story's acceptance criteria (the create and update database functions reject an empty or foreign criteria list, supabase/migrations/0021_atc_create_update.sql). Tests chain ATCs by reference, a Run freezes a copy of what it executed, and a bug keeps links to the run step and ATC it came from. That chain (criterion, ATC, Test, Run, Bug) is what the traceability and coverage reports read.

Target users

  • QA engineers and QA leads working inside a workspace, with the roles the database enforces: viewer, member, admin, owner (supabase/migrations/0001_tenancy.sql).
  • Programmatic operators (CLI, CI, AI agents) that authenticate with a Personal Access Token and may declare themselves as an agent or ci executor when they start a Run (supabase/migrations/0031_runs.sql, lib/api/middleware/bearer.ts).
  • Workspace owners who buy the paid tier (Billing Plan) and own data export and deletion.
  • Named personas in the docs (senior QA engineer, QA lead, developer, autonomous AI test agent) remain intent only (.context/PRD/executive-summary.md).

Value proposition (delivered at 98ee1b4)

  • Multi-tenant workspaces with roles, invite links, self-service leave, owner deletion with a 30-day restore window, and a full data export (route:/settings/workspaces, route:/settings/data-export).
  • An authoring tree: projects, modules (create, rename, move, archive), user stories with a Ready-to-test gate, ordered acceptance criteria, and a one-way Jira story import (components/layout/Sidebar.tsx, app/(app)/projects/[projectSlug]/import-from-jira-dialog.tsx).
  • An ATC library: create, edit, duplicate, search, export, classify by technique and priority, with mandatory anchoring (components/atcs/).
  • Tests as ordered chains of ATC references with suite tags, grouped into Test Plans; Milestones as dated targets (components/tests/, components/test-plans/, components/milestones/).
  • Execution: Runs of a Test against a project environment by a human, an agent or CI, with per-step verdicts, notes and evidence, live updates and an automatic close of abandoned runs (components/runs/RunnerView.tsx, supabase/migrations/0075_run_inactivity_sweep.sql).
  • Native bug tracking: severity, assignee, a forward-only status lifecycle, filed straight from a failed step (components/bugs/).
  • Quality reports: coverage per criterion and module, a story traceability chain, recovery cycles, a defect heatmap, a run report, Home widgets and a command palette (route:/projects/[projectSlug]/metrics, route:/projects/[projectSlug]/traceability).
  • A notification inbox and a daily email digest with per-user preferences (components/notifications/, route:/settings/notifications).
  • A versioned REST API with OpenAPI docs, scoped tokens and idempotency keys for non-browser callers (app/api/v1/, route:/api/docs).
  • Self-service upgrade from Community to Cloud through Stripe Checkout (route:/settings/billing/upgrade).

Main navigation: Home, Activity, Projects, ATC Library, Test Runs, Bug Reports, Metrics, Settings (components/layout/AppSidebar.tsx); inside a project: All ATCs, Test Runs, Bug Reports, Metrics, Traceability, Milestones, Test Plans (app/(app)/projects/[projectSlug]/project-sub-nav.tsx). The global entries ATC Library, Test Runs, Bug Reports and Metrics have no link of their own (href: null); they are reached inside a project.

Still not delivered, though the product glossary or docs describe them: chat channels, messages, mentions and rich links; a run "Execution Mode" (manual / automated) and a per-Test "Automation Status"; CI results upload; subscriptions, invoices and renewals; writing bugs back to Jira; closing a Test Plan; attaching Test Plans to a Milestone (see discovery gaps).

QA relevance

Business aspectTesting implication
Traceability is the core promiseAnchoring rules (story + at least one of its criteria) and the chain to Test, Run and Bug are the highest-value acceptance checks; a write that bypasses them breaks the product's reason to exist.
Multi-tenant workspacesCross-tenant leakage is the top business risk: negative tests per role and per workspace, including soft-deleted workspaces, which must read as non-existent.
API-first for agents and CIToken scopes, expiry, revocation and the executor mode a token may declare are business features: test them as such.
Self-service onboardingEmail-first sign-up, OAuth, magic link, first-workspace creation and invite acceptance are the activation funnel: smoke scope.
Coverage drives decisions"Uncovered" and "not run" must never merge; a skipped or blocked latest result counts as not run.
Paid tier and limitsOnly the project limit blocks; seat and retention limits are displayed but not enforced. Checkout must change the plan only on a confirmed Stripe payment.
Irreversible data actionsWorkspace deletion becomes permanent after 30 days; restore, export expiry and owner-only gates are high-consequence checks.

Workspace

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
WorkspaceWorkspace, workspace_id, bunkai_bootstrap_workspace"Workspace" (Create workspace, workspace switcher, Settings > Workspaces)workspacessupabase/migrations/0001_tenancy.sql, lib/types.ts, components/settings/WorkspacesList.tsx

Business meaning: the tenant and the billing unit. A team's private space; every project, Test, run, bug and notification belongs to exactly one workspace, and a person sees only the live workspaces they are an active member of. It has a globally unique URL slug, a name, one or more owners, a Billing Plan tier and, once paid, a purchased seat count. A workspace scheduled for deletion is treated by every access check as if it did not exist.

UI labels: onboarding form with name (placeholder "Acme QA") and slug (placeholder "acme-qa"), button "Create workspace", toast "Workspace created"; switcher toast "Workspace switched."; Settings > Workspaces list with "Leave" and "Delete" actions and toast "<name> was deleted." The active workspace is remembered in a cookie separate from the session (lib/api/workspace-cookie.ts).

Related terms: Workspace member, Workspace invite, Project, Billing Plan, Workspace export, Workspace deletion.

Abbreviations: ws (code helpers, e.g. bunkai_is_workspace_member(ws_id)).

Business meaning: a person's seat in a workspace, carrying their role (what they may do) and status (whether the seat is live). Only an active membership grants visibility; write access needs at least the member role; member management needs admin or owner. A workspace may have several owners. Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in

Business meaning: an admin's offer for one email address to join a workspace with a given role (never owner). Bunkai sends no invite email: the admin copies the link and shares it. The link expires after 7 days and can be revoked or rotated (a new link replaces the old). An email that already belongs to an active member cannot be invited. Accepting requires being signed in with that same email; it adds the membership or promotes a lower role, and is refused when the person already holds an equal or higher role.

UI labels: "Generate invite link", placeholder "teammate@company.com", "No invites yet.", toasts "Invite revoked.", "New invite link copied to clipboard."; accept page "Checking session…", "Joining workspace…", "Welcome — you have joined the workspace."; refusal "This invite was sent to a different email address."

Related terms: Workspace, Workspace member, Workspace deletion (revokes pending invites).

Abbreviations: none; say "invite link" or "invite token", never bare "token" (the product glossary reserves it).

Module

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
ModuleModule, ModuleTreeNode, parent_module_id, path, archived_at"Module", "New module", "New sub-module", folders in "Explorer"modulessupabase/migrations/0002_projects_modules.sql, supabase/migrations/0014_module_soft_delete.sql, lib/tree.ts

Business meaning: a functional area of the project (a feature or component), nestable into sub-modules up to six levels deep, identified by a slash path (for example auth/login), with an optional description of up to 500 characters. It is where user stories and ATCs live and the unit coverage and the defect heatmap aggregate by, which is why the product treats it as a first-class node, not a folder name. Modules can be renamed and moved; "deleting" a module archives it with its whole subtree (sub-modules, stories, criteria, ATCs), while runs and bugs stay readable.

UI labels: "Explorer" sidebar folders; context menu "New sub-module", "New user story", "Rename", "Move", "Delete"; buttons "New module", "Create your first module"; description placeholder "What this module covers."; "Delete module" dialog; toasts "Archived “<name>”", "Moved “<name>”"; "Module" column in the ATC table; "Select a module…" when filing a bug.

User story

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
User storyUserStory, UserStoryStatus, user_story_id, external_id, external_url"User story", "New user story", "Linked user story", "Draft" / "Ready to test"user_storiessupabase/migrations/0003_authoring.sql, supabase/migrations/0017_acceptance_criteria_ordering.sql, lib/types.ts

Business meaning: the requirement an ATC proves. It belongs to a module and may point to the same story in an external tracker (a Jira key, unique per project among active stories, and a URL); stories can be typed in or imported from Jira. It carries a Ready-to-test gate: "Ready to test" is the explicit signal that its criteria are settled, needs at least one active criterion, and falls back to "Draft" when the last criterion is removed. The gate is a two-state signal, not a workflow, and blocks nothing else. A story with ATCs cannot be hard-deleted; removing it archives it.

UI labels: Explorer menu "New user story", "Edit", "Manage criteria", "Remove", "Copy ID"; form placeholders "Refund a paid order", "BK-42" (Jira key), "Describe the story in Markdown."; note "The Jira link is set and cannot be changed."; gate badge "Draft" / "Ready to test", actions "Mark ready to test" / "Back to draft", toasts "Marked ready to test", "Story moved back to draft — it has no criteria left."; ATC editor panel "Linked user story" with search placeholder "Search US- or paste a Jira ID…".

ATC

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
ATC (Acceptance Test Case)Atc, AtcLayer, AtcTechnique, AtcPriority, bunkai_create_atc, bunkai_update_atc"ATC", "All ATCs", "ATC Library", "New ATC", "ATC created", "ATC saved"atcssupabase/migrations/0004_atcs.sql, supabase/migrations/0021_atc_create_update.sql, components/atcs/AtcEditor.tsx

Business meaning: the product's central unit of authorship: one small, reusable verification of a single observable behaviour, written as ordered steps plus assertions, placed in a module, tagged (at most 10 tags), classified by test layer and optionally by test-design technique and ATC Priority, and anchored to a user story and its criteria. Every save bumps its version and is refused when someone else saved first. Tests reference ATCs instead of copying them, so one edit updates every Test that chains it ("one edit, many tests"). An ATC can be duplicated, searched and exported; it has no delete and is archived only with its module.

Execution status: the atcs.status column (pass / fail / blocked / skipped / running / unrun) is still shown as a status dot, but no code path writes it, so every ATC reads unrun. Real results live on the run step; coverage and traceability read those.

UI labels: editor fields "Title" (required, at least 3 characters, placeholder "A single observable behaviour — start with a verb"), "Module", "Layer", "Technique", "Priority" ("Not specified" when unset), "Steps", "Assertions", "Tags", "Linked user story", panel state "Anchored"; toasts "ATC created", "ATC duplicated", "ATC saved — N Tests updated"; "Used by" (the Tests that chain it); table filters "All techniques", "All priorities"; "ATC library exported"; empty state "No Acceptance Test Case has been written for this project yet."

Naming: ATC = Acceptance Test Case everywhere in current code, metadata, login page and schema (app/layout.tsx, app/(auth)/login/page.tsx, supabase/migrations/0004_atcs.sql). The product glossary bans "Atomic Test Component" (.context/business/domain-glossary.md §0, §4). ATC Priority (Critical / High / Medium / Low) is a different scale from Bug Severity and from Jira priority.

Related terms: ATC step, ATC assertion, Anchoring, Module, User story, Test. Values: ATC layer, ATC status, ATC technique, ATC priority.

Anchoring

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Anchoring (ATC to criteria binding)AtcAcceptanceCriterion, isAnchored, p_ac_ids, error ac_outside_user_story"Anchored" (anchoring panel)atc_acceptance_criteria (many-to-many) + atcs.user_story_idsupabase/migrations/0004_atcs.sql, supabase/migrations/0021_atc_create_update.sql, components/atcs/AnchoringPanel.tsx

Business meaning: the traceability rule that defines the product: an ATC is anchored when it names one user story and at least one active criterion of that story. The editor will not save an unanchored ATC, and the create and update database functions refuse an empty criteria list or any criterion outside the story. The story of an ATC cannot change after creation. Anchoring is what coverage and the traceability chain read.

UI labels: save hints "Pick a User Story to enable Save", "Bind at least one Acceptance Criterion to enable Save"; server messages "Bind to a user story before saving.", "Bind at least one acceptance criterion."

Personal access token

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Personal access tokenaccess_tokens, mintPat, token_prefix, scopes"Personal access tokens", "New token", "Revoke token"access_tokens (+ hash in access_token_secrets)supabase/migrations/0008_access_tokens.sql, lib/api/pat.ts, components/settings/IssueTokenModal.tsx

Business meaning: a long-lived credential that lets a CLI, CI job or AI agent call the API as its owner, limited by scopes and optionally bound to one workspace; it never exceeds the owner's own permissions, and the workspace:admin scope can only be granted on a workspace where the owner is admin or owner. Shown in full once at creation (bk_pat_<prefix>.<secret>), never retrievable again. Issued and revoked from Settings in a browser session (or returned by the headless sign-in endpoints); a token cannot mint or revoke tokens. Revocation keeps the row for audit; leaving or deleting a workspace revokes the tokens bound to it.

UI labels: Settings > "Personal access tokens" ("Authenticate the Bunkai CLI and your CI against your account."), "Your tokens", "New token" / "Issue your first token", dialog "New personal access token" with "Token name" (placeholder "ci-deploy", "Lowercase and hyphens. Names the machine that will use it."), "Scopes", "Workspace — optional", "Expiry — optional" ("No expiry"); "Revoke token", toast "Token revoked".

Idempotency key

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Idempotency keyidempotency_keys, header Idempotency-Key, error codes idempotency_key_required / idempotency_key_invalidnone (API header)idempotency_keyssupabase/migrations/0009_cross_cutting.sql, lib/api/idempotency.ts

Business meaning: a client-chosen key that makes a repeated create request return the first result instead of creating a duplicate, kept per user and endpoint. It is required on four endpoints: create a Test, start a Run, add Tests to a Test Plan, and start a billing checkout. Reusing a key with a different body, or while the first request is still in flight, is refused. Starting a Run has a second, domain-level guard: the same Test and start token within 24 hours returns the existing Run.

Related terms: Test, Run, Test Plan, Billing checkout. Values: idempotency status.

Structure: business-data-context section entities (Idempotency key row).

Test

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Test (chain of ATCs)tests, test_steps (chain step: test_id, atc_id, position), bunkai_create_test"Test", "New Test", "Steps", "Run History", "Suites:"tests, test_stepssupabase/migrations/0024_tests.sql, supabase/migrations/0030_test_tags.sql, components/tests/NewTestBuilder.tsx

Business meaning: the unit of execution: a named, ordered chain of references to ATCs that walks one journey (an end-to-end or integration scenario). It holds references, not copies, so an ATC edit shows up in every Test that chains it; the same ATC may appear at several positions, so a chain position is addressed by its own chain-step id, not by the ATC. A Test belongs to the workspace, not to one project (its project is derived from the ATCs it chains), needs at least one ATC, a title of 1 to 200 characters, and can be reordered (same ATCs, new order) and tagged. Three reserved suite tags, smoke, sanity, regression, are lower-cased; custom tags keep their casing (at most 20, each up to 50 characters). Tests have no delete.

UI labels: "New Test", title placeholder "Name the journey this chain verifies", "Filter ATCs…", "A Test must include at least one ATC.", toast "Test created"; tabs "Steps" and "Run History"; "Chain order changed — unsaved.", toast "Chain reordered"; "Suites:" quick-add, toast "Tags updated."; "Start run" with an "Environment…" picker, toast "Run started"; ATC side "Used by".

Related terms: ATC, Run, Test Plan, Environment, Idempotency key.

Abbreviations: the product glossary maps the methodology's TC (Test Case) to a Bunkai Test and bans calling a chain "test case" or "test component" (.context/business/domain-glossary.md §1, §4).

Business meaning: a curated group of Tests inside one project for a goal, cycle or release. It has a name (1 to 100 characters, unique per project ignoring case), a goal or release (up to 100) and a description (up to 500). A Test joins a plan at most once and may belong to several plans; only Tests whose whole chain lies in the plan's project can be added, and removing a Test from a plan only removes the membership. A plan is created Open and is editable only while Open; nothing in the product closes it yet.

UI labels: project section "Test Plans", "New plan", "Create first plan", empty state "No test plans yet"; list columns "Name", "Goal / release", "Status", "Tests", "Created by"; placeholders "e.g. Release 2.4 regression", "Release 2.4", "What this plan covers and when it should run"; "Add tests" picker ("Filter by name or tag", "No tests match."), "This plan has no tests yet", "Remove from this plan"; status chip "Open" / "Closed"; toast "Test plan details updated".

Run

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Run (test run, execution)runs, executor_mode, start_token, abort_reason, bunkai_create_run"Test Runs", "Start run", "Finish run", "Abort run", "Run History"runs (+ run_atcs, run_steps)supabase/migrations/0031_runs.sql, components/runs/RunnerView.tsx

Business meaning: one execution of a Test against a project environment, by a human, an agent or CI. At start it freezes a copy of the Test's chain (every ATC position and every step), so later ATC edits never change the evidence. The executor marks each run step, then closes the Run with a verdict they choose (passed or failed), or aborts it with a reason. Only a running Run accepts marks; a closed Run is final. A Run with no step activity for 4 hours is closed automatically as aborted ("Auto-closed by inactivity sweep"). The starter is notified when it finishes or aborts, unless they closed it themselves in the browser. Runs have no delete.

UI labels: project section "Test Runs" (run report with filters, "All modules"); "Start run", toast "Run started"; runner "Finish run", "Abort run" with "Abort reason" (placeholder "Why are you aborting this run?"), toasts "Run finished", "Run aborted"; status labels "Running", "Passed", "Failed", "Aborted"; executor labels "Human", "Agent", "CI" (the Home active-runs panel says "Manual" for human).

Related terms: Test, Environment, Run step, Bug, Notification, Coverage. Values: run status, run executor mode.

Run step

Business nameCode identifierUI labelTable / collectionFound in
Run step (step result) and run ATC (position result)run_steps (status, note, evidence_url), run_atcs, bunkai_mark_run_step"Pass" / "Fail" / "Block", "Step marked", "Unrun"run_steps, run_atcssupabase/migrations/0031_runs.sql, supabase/migrations/0042_run_step_mark.sql, lib/runs/mark-step-view.ts

Business meaning: the frozen copy of one ATC step inside a Run, and the verdict recorded on it: passed, failed or blocked, with an optional note and evidence link. A marked step can be re-marked while the Run is running (last mark wins, no history). Each chain position (run ATC) carries its own verdict derived from its steps; this per-ATC result is what coverage and traceability read as an ATC's real execution status. When the Run is closed, every step still pending becomes skipped. A failed step is where a bug is filed from.

Grain: the product glossary separates three run vocabularies: the Run (running / passed / failed / aborted), the position and step (pending / passed / failed / blocked / skipped), and the traceability chip that combines both. aborted exists only at the Run grain (.context/business/domain-glossary.md §3).

UI labels: mark buttons "Pass", "Fail", "Block"; note placeholder "What did you observe?", evidence placeholder "https://…"; toast "Step marked"; verdict badges "Unrun" (stored pending), "Passed", "Failed", "Blocked", "Skipped"; "Report bug" on a failed step.

Related terms: Run, ATC step, Bug, Coverage. Values: run step status.

Bug

Business meaning: a defect tracked natively inside Bunkai, not delegated to Jira. It always belongs to a project and a module, and is either filed from a failed run step (the run, step and ATC are linked automatically as its origin) or filed manually with no origin. It has a title (5 to 200 characters), a severity, an optional description and steps to reproduce, up to 10 evidence links, a reporter and an optional assignee, who must be an active member above viewer. Its status moves one stage forward at a time and never back. Bugs have no delete and stay readable after their module is archived (tagged "Archived").

Severity: stored as P1 to P4, rendered as words: P1 Critical, P2 Major, P3 Minor, P4 Trivial (lib/bugs/constants.ts). Not the same scale as ATC Priority.

UI labels: project section "Bug Reports" with List and Heatmap views; "New bug" / "Report bug" dialog ("What went wrong?", "Select a module…", "File bug"), toast "Bug filed"; detail "Origin", "Details", "Evidence", "Steps to reproduce", "Filed manually. This defect was reported directly — no test run or ATC is linked.", "Unassigned"; one forward action per status: "Start progress", "Mark resolved", "Close"; toast "Bug status updated".

Related terms: Run step, Module, ATC, Defect heatmap, Notification, Traceability chain. Values: bug severity, bug status.

Abbreviations: the product glossary distinguishes Defect (any deviation) from Bug (found during execution); the UI uses "Bug" and the traceability view "Defects".

Business meaning: how much of a project's acceptance criteria is backed by tests that actually ran. Per criterion: uncovered when no live ATC of the project is bound to it (an authoring gap); not run when a bound ATC's most recent result is anything but passed or failed, including never run, skipped and blocked (an execution gap); otherwise executed. A failed ATC still counts as coverage: coverage and health are separate axes. A module rolls up as no criteria, uncovered, not run or fully covered. The two gaps have different owners and must never be merged into one "not covered" state. Shown on the project Metrics page and summarised on Home; also available per workspace.

UI labels: "Coverage by module", "Executed vs. bound-but-never-run vs. unbound acceptance criteria", "Coverage gaps", "No coverage gaps.", "Zero linked ATCs: nothing bound at all", "Never run" (Home says "awaiting execution" for the same state; the product glossary records this drift).

Related terms: Acceptance criterion, Anchoring, Run step, Module, Traceability chain. Values: coverage state, module coverage status.

Business meaning: the evidence chain for one user story, read in one screen: each acceptance criterion, the ATCs bound to it, the Tests that chain those ATCs, their latest Runs and the bugs they produced. Each run row reads in flight (run still running or ATC still pending), aborted, or the ATC's result. It names three distinct absences: "Uncovered" (a criterion with no ATC), "No test written yet", "No run recorded yet". It can be exported as a snapshot. The product glossary separates this chain (criterion, ATC, Test, Run, Defect) from the methodology's traceability (US, ATP, ATR, TC); say which one is meant.

Business meaning: per user story, the time from its first failing run to the first later run in which it fully passes: how long a broken story stayed broken. It measures repair latency, not defect count, and is computed from run data only. A story with run history reads Recovered, Not yet green (failed, not yet passing again) or No cycle (never failed). Shown on the project Metrics page with the project median. The product glossary asks to never shorten it to "recovery".

Business meaning: bugs per active module over a rolling window of 7, 30 or 90 days, with a week-over-week trend. A parent module counts its descendants' bugs, including bugs filed against modules archived since. Each module gets a heat level: Clean (0), Low (up to 2), Elevated (up to 4), Hotspot (more than 4); the trend reads Rising, Falling or Flat. It is the second view of the Bug Reports screen and the reason modules are first-class.

UI labels: "Window", "Trend compares the latest 7 days vs. the prior 7 days", "Includes all nested sub-modules", heat labels "Clean", "Low", "Elevated", "Hotspot", trend "Rising", "Falling", "Flat"; empty state "No active modules in this Project".

Business meaning: a message in one member's inbox about a run or bug event that concerns them. Produced automatically from the activity log: the run starter when their Run finishes or aborts (not when they closed it themselves in the browser); the new assignee when a bug is assigned or reassigned; the reporter and assignee when a bug's status changes, never the person who changed it. Each recipient gets at most one per event. The inbox shows the last 90 days, updates live, and keeps an item readable as "This item is no longer available." when its entity is gone or hidden. Business meaning: an owner's request to erase a workspace. Owner only, from a browser session; other members cannot veto. From that moment the workspace is invisible to everyone, its tokens and pending invites are revoked, and the owner and every active member get an email with a restore link. For 30 days the owner can restore it (data intact, revoked tokens and invites stay revoked); after that a daily job deletes it permanently. A tombstone record (name, slug, requester, member count, row counts) survives the purge for audit.

Business meaning: the subscription tier of a workspace, which sets its limits and price. Community: free, 5 seats, 3 projects, 30-day retention. Cloud: 24.00 USD per seat, 25 seats, 50 projects, 90-day retention. Enterprise: custom price, no limits. A seat is one active member counted against the tier. Only the project limit is enforced (project creation is refused above it); seats and retention are shown as usage meters and never block. Admins and owners see the billing overview; only the owner can upgrade (see Billing checkout). There is no downgrade, renewal date or invoice.

UI labels: Settings > "Billing" ("Plan, seats, and usage for this workspace."), "Current plan", "Seats", "Usage", "Run history" (retention meter), "Upgrade plan", "Unable to load billing info"; Community shows "No active subscription".

Naming: the stored values are community / cloud / enterprise; the product glossary bans "Free / Team / Enterprise" and bare "plan" (collides with Test Plan) (.context/business/domain-glossary.md §3, §4).

Related terms: Workspace, Workspace member, Project, Billing checkout. Values: workspace plan.

Discovery gaps

The following items could not be verified from code, or code and docs disagree, and require human confirmation:

  • Docs ahead of code. The product glossary (.context/business/domain-glossary.md, last code-synced at 4924f48) defines terms with no table, route or screen at 98ee1b4: Channel, Message, Mention, Rich Link, Execution Mode (manual / automated), Automation Status (manual-only / candidate / automated), CI Results File, Subscription, Invoice, and a one-way bug sync to Jira. No term- section was written for them. Whether they are still planned is a product question.
  • Glossary vs code on environments. The product glossary says Staging and Production are seeded per project; the code seeded them only once, for projects that existed when runs shipped (supabase/migrations/0031_runs.sql), and new projects start with none, so they cannot run a Test until someone adds an environment. Intended behaviour unconfirmed.
  • Dead execution status on ATCs. atcs.status is displayed (status dot, sidebar filter "fail / blocked / unrun") but never written, so it always reads unrun even after Runs. Whether it should mirror the latest run result is unconfirmed.
  • Assertions are not part of a Run. Runs snapshot ATC steps only; assertions are neither copied nor shown in the runner, although the editor describes them as "checked by every executor". How an executor is meant to apply them is unconfirmed.
  • Limits shown but not enforced. Seat and retention limits appear as usage meters; invites and acceptance do not check seats and nothing deletes old runs. Only the project limit blocks. Whether enforcement is planned is a product question.
  • Billing lifecycle. Only the Cloud upgrade exists. No downgrade, cancellation, renewal, failed-renewal or invoice handling; Enterprise has no path that sets it. Revenue figures beyond the per-seat price are not in code.
  • Unreachable values. Test plan closed, member status invited and suspended, and the mentions preference have no path that sets or uses them; their meaning is inferred from names and docs.
  • In-app preference has no effect. The "In-app" switch is stored but notification producers ignore it; only "Email" filters the digest.
  • Milestone to Test Plan link. The milestone screen says attaching plans "arrives with a later capability"; nothing links them yet.
  • Label drift (unruled). Executor human renders "Human" in run lists and "Manual" on Home; a bound-but-never-run criterion renders "Never run" on Metrics and "awaiting execution" on Home; run verdicts render "Passed" / "Pass". Recorded as unruled in the product glossary §5. The global sidebar entries ATC Library, Test Runs, Bug Reports and Metrics have no link of their own.
  • Unused schema. feature_flags and user_view_state still have no reader or writer in app code.
  • Structure pointers on unchanged sections. term-feature-flag and term-view-state were left byte-identical and still read "pending (data map placeholder)"; the business-data-context map now exists and holds both in its entities section.
  • Revenue Streams and Cost Structure beyond the Cloud price rest on the business doc only (Low confidence).
  • No i18n bundle. UI labels come from component JSX; the QA guide page (app/qa/) is in Spanish while the app UI is in English. Confirm the product's official UI language.
  • Diagrams. No figure drawn: this map is tables by design (figures are optional here); a relationship overview can be added later after the diagrams capability check.
